I’m an old hand at this now, 36 years on these fields. I can’t take big chances. Two people in the house means labor is tight, and 15 mu is not so much that I can waste land, but not so little that I plant only one thing. Wheat and maize are the steady pair here, everybody does it, and it keeps grain coming. Cotton gives cash if the year is decent, so I will still keep a small piece in cotton, but not too much because cotton takes more looking after and more picking by hand. I will mostly do what worked before: wheat on the bigger part, then maize right after harvest, and a smaller piece of cotton on its own. Fertilizer I won’t cut too hard, because if the crop turns yellow and thin, that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. But I also won’t go too heavy because cash must stay in hand for water, medicine, and emergencies.

For wheat, I like to get it in around early October, not too late, with the local seed I can get nearby. I usually put base fertilizer before sowing, then another bit when the wheat starts standing up strong in spring. If the winter and spring are dry, I use the well two or three times, but I watch the pumping cost. After wheat harvest in June, the maize must go in fast, no delay, maybe in two or three days, because if you miss moisture and heat, yield drops. Maize I keep simpler, one base application and one topdress if it looks good enough to deserve it. Cotton I plant on the smaller patch in April. Cotton needs more watching for worms and more hand work, so I keep only a few mu. I will not chase the highest yield. I want a steady year, enough grain, some cash from cotton, and not too much spending.
